name: CT-01
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+12 partisan lean combined with a Democratic-favorable national environment
Luke Bronin's overwhelming financial edge: $3.1M raised and $900K in outside support versus roughly $21K for Amy Chai
Open seat after John Larson's renomination loss removes incumbency but not the district's structural Democratic advantage
Prediction markets price a Democratic win at roughly 95%
model.rationale: The D+12 district and a favorable environment point to a Democratic hold, and Bronin's massive fundraising and outside-spending advantage over Chai reinforces that picture. With no polls showing a contest and markets pricing a Democratic win near certainty, an open seat is the only factor tempering the margin slightly below the fundamentals-based estimate.
model.watch: Any late general-election polling showing Chai within single digits, or an unexpected scandal involving Bronin, would be the main signals to revisit this rating.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: John B. Larson (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Connecticut's first district is a Democratic-leaning seat, and the retirement of long-time incumbent John Larson after his renomination loss hands the nomination to former Hartford mayor Luke Bronin. He faces Republican Amy Chai, a physician and first-time candidate, in a district that has reliably elected Democrats.

The resource picture is lopsided: Bronin has raised about $3.1 million and benefits from roughly $900,000 in outside support, while Chai has raised about $21,000 with minimal cash on hand. Prediction markets give Democrats roughly a 95 percent chance of holding the seat. With no public polling and no expert ratings, the forecast rests on the district's D+12 lean, a Democratic-favorable environment, and the stark money gap, all pointing to a comfortable Democratic hold.
